text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Ben Verwaayen to step down as managing director of PTT Telecom on September 1. (p1)
- Computer hardware and services chain Computer Company seeks bourse listing. (p1)
- Philips Electronics refuses to bear the full Dfl 631 losses of stake in Germany's Grundig. (p3)
- Supermarkets angry over high tariffs of financial traffic. (p5)
- MPs were fully informed about technolease deals between certain companies and banks in 1993/1994. (p7)
VOLKSKRANT
- Cabinet plans higher taxes on company cars. (p1)
- Investors angry at banks' refusal to reveal size of oversubscriptions to animal food group Nutreco's float. (p2)
- Small businesses association MKB calls for tax reduction.
DE TELEGRAAF
- Truck maker DAF just able to meet growing demand. (p3)
- FNV union wants to slash 2,000 jobs in pig slaughter houses to keep them competitive. (p9)
- Trade with Germany stagnated in 1996. (p23)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Fiscal advantage for lowest earners should create some 78,000 jobs, according to research institute Nyfer. (p10)
TROUW
- Majority in parliament opposes junior justice minister's return policy for asylum seekers. (p1)
- Employers' association VNO-NCW estimates introduction of the euro will cost several billion guilders. (p7)
